newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks slump on futures sales after glitch.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks slump on futures sales after glitch.

text.p: Tokyo stocks slumped to end more than two percent lower on Friday after a technical glitch which halted electronic-system trades on the Tokyo bourse throughout the morning brought on shower of arbitrage-linked sales when trading resumed after the lunch break, brokers said.
They added that the losses were exacerbated by market participants who sold stock futures in exchange for bond futures in the afternoon session.
Hitachi Ltd, the most heavily traded issue with 14.49 million shares, hit a new high for the year of 1,390 yen before ending at 1,360, up 20 yen.

Sony Corp surged to an all-time high of 12,600 yen, cheered by robust growth in its first-quarter earnings which were announced Thursday. It ended up 400 at 12,200. "The two-tiered trend should continue as the yen is weak against the dollar, which is good for those high-tech firms that are competitive with overseas firms," said Noboru Yorita, Tachibana Securities general manager. "The only cloud is anxiety over the bull run of U.S. stocks, which could falter any day."

Nomura Securities Co Ltd hit a new high for this calendar year of 1,740 before closing unchanged at 1,680 as relieved investors bought the shares after long-awaited administrative penalties for its role in a racketeer scandal were finally announced on Wednesday.
Yamaichi Securities rebounded, adding 10 yen to 270, on what brokers said was solely technical short-covering.

"The worst is over for Nomura but the investigation is just starting for Yamaichi and no one knows what will happen," one broker said. "It is financially weaker than Nomura, which means it may have more difficulty if penalties are administered."
Brokers said the Nikkei's downside was seen at around 19,500 in coming sessions.
"The benchmark fell, but looking at individual shares, blue chips were firm," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
"Hedging needs and loss-cutting sales picked up in the futures market, sending the Nikkei average lower, so there really isn't much need for pessimism," he said.
By sector, only services posted major gains. Fisheries, warehouses, land transport, mining and real estate topped the list of retreaters.

The TOPIX index fell 31.25 points or 2.02 percent to 1,512.79. The Nikkei 300 shed 6.44 points or 2.13 percent to 295.49. The second-section index lost 6.72 points or 0.38 percent to end at 1,762.57. Second-section turnover was 7.67 million shares compared to 9.34 million on the previous day.
The over-the-counter index was down 6.47 points or 0.57 percent at 1,118.88 in late Tokyo afternoon, down for the 25th straight session.
